title: Efficient protocol for the Markovian Mpemba effect in $N$-level systems
abstract: The Mpemba effect is an anomalous phenomenon in which the time to thermalize does not depend monotonically on the distance from equilibrium, allowing systems with an initially larger temperature difference to thermalize before those with a smaller one. The rarity of the effect makes it hard to find parameters that produce it, complicating the design of experiments and the development of applications. Here, we find necessary and sufficient conditions for the Markovian Mpemba effect in three-level systems and explain its underlying physical mechanisms. Based on our understanding of the three-level case, we develop an efficient algorithm to determine the parameters for the effect in $N$-level systems. This protocol could open the door for the realization of Mpemba experiments and related applications in large systems.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive theoretical framework to understand the Markovian Mpemba effect in $N$-level quantum systems. By first solving the problem for three-level systems, the authors develop an efficient protocol to predict the conditions required for the effect in larger systems. This work advances the understanding of non-monotonic thermalization dynamics in quantum matter.
main_problem: The paper investigates the necessary and sufficient conditions for the Markovian Mpemba effect in general $N$-level quantum systems.
main_result: The authors derive specific conditions for 3-level systems and propose an efficient Single Pair of States Deviation (SPSD) protocol to determine parameters for the effect in larger $N$-level systems.
method: The analysis uses the Pauli rate equation, eigenvalue analysis of the transition matrix, and develops a systematic protocol based on analyzing low-dimensional subsystems (triplets).
model_or_system: The study focuses on $N$-level quantum systems undergoing thermalization, modeled by the Pauli rate equation ($\dot{P} = MP$). Initial analysis is performed on three-level systems (3LSs) to establish general criteria.
key_observables: The existence and nature (direct vs. inverse) of the Markovian Mpemba effect, diagnosed via the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the transition matrix.
important_parameters: The bath inverse temperature ($ eta_b$), energy level spacing ratios ($r$), and renormalized transition rates ($	ilde{a}_{23}, 	ilde{a}_{13}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Markovian approximation and assumes detailed balance for the transition rates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the population state locus in 3LSs, plot the probability of the Mpemba effect versus bath temperature for $N=3, 4, 5$, and show success rates for the SPSD protocol as a function of $ eta_b$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for 3LSs using geometric and spectral analysis. It then generalizes this understanding by developing the SPSD protocol to efficiently map the parameter space for arbitrary $N$-level systems, showing the dependence on temperature.
why_interesting: The Mpemba effect is a non-monotonic thermalization anomaly, making this work highly relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and the study of relaxation dynamics in open quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Each point inside the triangle represents a state of the 3LS population, {p1, p2, p3}. The corners are pure states of levels 1, 2 or 3, respectively. The thermal states are repre- sented by one of the color lines, whose shape depends on the energy level distribution through r.

FIG. 2. Probability for N-level Markovian Mpemba effect as a function of the normalized bath inverse temperature. We considered bounded values of transition rates (0 < aij < 1). As shown in the plot, the probability decreases with bath tem- perature. 3-, 4-, and 5-level systems are shown in the figure. The convergence of the results was assessed by increasing the number of realizations and confirming that this did not signif- icantly alter the plot. For the transition rates, we considered values from 0.001 to 1 and for βbϵi from 0 to 5N. Each point in the graphs is based in 106 random realizations.

FIG. 4. Markovian Mpemba effect for the lowest three hydrogen-like energy levels, r < 1, as a function of the normal- ized transition rates. The upper plots show the area (in dark blue) of Mechanism 4, the only mechanism for the Markovian Mpemba effect for r < 1. The bottom plots show the region of the inverse Markovian Mpemba effect (yellow) and the direct Markovian Mpemba effect (blue). Each plot column corre- sponds to a different βb. See Figure 3 for other details of the color coding. The energy levels are (arbitrary units): -5,-5/4,- 5/9.

FIG. 3. Markovian Mpemba effect for the lowest three rota- tional energy levels, r > 1, as a function of the normalized transition rates. The upper plots show the different mecha- nisms: Mechanism 1 (red), Mechanism 2 (light orange), and Mechanism 3 (Dark orange). The lower plots show the regions of the inverse (yellow) and direct (blue) Markovian Mpemba effect. In all plots, the purple regions correspond to parame- ter values without the Markovian Mpemba effect, and a black point represents the singular point. Each plot column corre- sponds to a different βb. The energy levels are 2, 6 and 12 (in arbitrary units).

FIG. 5. Probability of a 4-level system exhibiting the Marko- vian Mpemba effect as a function of how many of its triplets exhibit any of the 3LS Markovian Mpemba mechanisms. No- tice that even in the case that all the triplets keep one of the 3LS mechanisms, the 4-level system may not exhibit the Markovian Mpemba effect. In this case, the probability is ∼93%. The convergence of the results was assessed by in- creasing the number of realizations and confirming that this did not significantly alter the plot. For the transition rates, we considered values from 0.001 to 1 and for βbϵi from 0 to 5. 5 × 105 realizations were used for the whole plot.
